anomalies.observed: The MAX3485 fail-safe/bias network is connected with opposite polarity: R8 (2.2k) pulls U1 pin 7 B toward +3V3, while R15 (2.2k) pulls U1 pin 6 A / the TTL servo bus toward GND. The TTL bus is on pin 6 A, so the idle differential is A low and B high.
anomalies.expected: For an idle-high UART/RS-485 half-duplex bus, the A line (the TTL bus in this schematic) should be pulled up and the B line pulled down, or the bias network should be reversed if the bus were on B. This gives a positive A-B idle differential and a high receiver output (RXD2) when the bus is idle.

evidence.quote: R6, R7, R8, R15 Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line.
Inferred: the bias/fail-safe purpose of the A/B line pull resistors (R6, R8, R15) on the MAX3485.

anomalies.impact: In serial-servo mode the MAX3485 receiver output will be held low when the bus is idle, and the driver differential will not produce the expected idle-high UART state. RXD2 would appear to be in a break/low state, preventing reliable half-duplex serial communication with the servos.

parsed.summary: Most of the schematic matches the specification, but the MAX3485 A/B bias/fail-safe resistors appear to be connected with reversed polarity, which would make the serial servo bus idle low and break UART communication.
